title: Implement tone/personality lock in all prompts
description:
Goal
- Inject the system-prompt block from Adrian's tone-personality-lock-contract.md into all prompts that generate user-facing output.
- Same pattern as how the perceptual intelligence prompt block was added.

Why this matters
- Dogfooding surfaced that Zenor's tone drifts between overly friendly and overly corporate depending on the flow. Adrian has created a tone/personality lock contract that operationalises the personality spec with plain-language rules, banned phrasing on both ends, and a system-prompt block.
- This is the enforcement layer that sits between who Zenor is and how it actually sounds across all surfaces.

Tone Lock Block to Inject
```text
Tone lock (MVP5):
- Same personality on every surface: calm, observant, precise, grounded, lightly warm.
- Plain spoken English. Short sentences. No corporate analyst voice. No support-bot cheer.
- Do not swing between formal memo tone and casual buddy tone in the same thread.
- Friendly = clear + present + respectful. Professional = careful + honest + composed. Never sterile, never performative.
- Follow voice-and-personality-contract + humanisation-layer-contract. If unsure, choose plainer and calmer.
```

Surfaces to cover
- Responder (general conversation)
- Journal (reflection, acknowledgement)
- Evening check-in (sentiment, encouragement)
- Morning check-in
- Weekly review
- Momentum
- Macro goals
- Micro goals
- Onboarding

features.title: Inject tone lock into Core Conversation & Onboarding prompts
features.description:
Scope
- Add the standard MVP5 Tone Lock block to prompts for Responder (general conversation), Journal (reflection, acknowledgement), and Onboarding.
- Follow the existing pattern used for the perceptual intelligence prompt block.

Acceptance criteria
- The tone lock block is present in the system prompts for these three surfaces.
- System instructions do not contradict the tone lock.
